content: Complexity-Constraint Code Evaluation research shows most LLMs (except top-tier) fail to recognize when a target complexity is infeasible for a problem, i.e. they will assert an achievable-sounding complexity even when no algorithm meeting it exists, rather than flagging infeasibility. This means a Reviewer accepting a complexity claim at face value without checking that the claimed complexity is achievable for the problem class is a known failure mode. No mature open tooling exists for automated complexity verification without execution; the practical mitigation used by teams is a structured review step that requires the algorithm's structure (loop nesting, recursion depth/branching, data structure operation costs) to be walked through and matched to the claim, not just accept an LLM-stated Big-O string.
